subsystems.name: Swarm elements
subsystems.role: each unit collects starlight, converts it to coherent light and emits it as one cell of a giant phased array.

subsystems.name: Phase and timing network
subsystems.role: keeps every element locked to a single reference so their beams add rather than cancel.
parts: metrology to measure each element's position to a fraction of a wavelength

subsystems.name: Emitter aperture
subsystems.role: the combined output — the array's effective aperture is the width of the swarm's orbit, so beam divergence falls with distance between the outermost elements.

subsystems.name: Power, cooling and mass
subsystems.role: handling stellar-scale power in a thin structure that must also survive solar radiation pressure.

subsystems.name: Orbit control
subsystems.role: holds the swarm in stable, non-colliding formation while the array is precisely phased.

subsystems.name: Command and safety
subsystems.role: computes firing solutions and can interrupt the beam.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate coherent combination on orbit
buildSteps.detail: Fly a few separate spacecraft, or one small optical phased array, and prove that several emitters can be locked together so their light adds in phase.

buildSteps.title: Extend the baseline
buildSteps.detail: Push the spacing between combined elements from metres to kilometres, while measuring and correcting the optical path to a fraction of a wavelength.

buildSteps.title: Build flight formation
buildSteps.detail: Fly dozens to hundreds of free-flying elements in a controlled formation that holds position against solar radiation pressure and orbital drift.

buildSteps.title: Mass-produce swarm elements
buildSteps.detail: A full array needs an almost unimaginable number of units — covering a sphere at Earth's distance from the Sun with kilometre-scale collectors would take hundreds of billions of them — so they would have to be made in space from asteroid or lunar material rather than launched.

buildSteps.title: Populate the orbit shell
buildSteps.detail: Spread the elements across one or more inclined orbital rings so the swarm stays gravitationally stable and does not shade or collide with itself.

buildSteps.title: Lock the whole array
buildSteps.detail: Run the master clock over the full network, calibrating each element's clock, position and phase until the swarm behaves as one telescope.

buildSteps.title: First full-aperture firing
buildSteps.detail: Aim the combined beam at a test target, such as a distant lightsail, and measure the spot it makes. Diffraction is the whole point: with an aperture of one astronomical unit and visible light, the spot at one light year is only tens of centimetres across.

buildSteps.title: Operate and expand
buildSteps.detail: Steer the beam, add elements, and manage the waste heat and station-keeping that continuous operation demands.

prerequisites.tech: Coherent beam combining and optical phased arrays
prerequisites.why: combining many emitters into one beam is done in the lab and in small photonic chips, but not between free-flying spacecraft.

solar sails have flown (JAXA's IKAROS in 2010, the Planetary Society's LightSail 2 in 2019), and a ground-based phased laser array of the order of 100 gigawatts was proposed by Breakthrough Starshot in 2016 to push gram-scale sails to about a fifth of light speed.
LISA Pathfinder proved free-fall laser metrology between separate spacecraft in 2015; a beam array needs the same precision across far longer baselines.
the sheer mass of a swarm cannot be launched from Earth economically; it would have to be built in orbit.
converting a large share of a star's output means radiating comparable waste heat from thin structures.
billions of orbiting elements interacting gravitationally and by radiation pressure have never been modelled or maintained.

pathway.milestone: lab-scale phased arrays, flown solar sails and free-flying laser metrology
pathway.unlocks: the component techniques, but each proven separately and at tiny scale.

pathway.milestone: a laser-driven lightsail accelerated to a few per cent of light speed
pathway.unlocks: interstellar probe concepts and confidence that beamed propulsion works.

pathway.milestone: kilometre-baseline arrays of tens of spacecraft held in phase
pathway.unlocks: apertures large enough to focus light over interplanetary distances.

pathway.milestone: in-space manufacturing grows the array from asteroid material
pathway.unlocks: apertures of millions of kilometres — beam spots of a few kilometres at a light year.

pathway.milestone: a phase-locked swarm spanning an orbit, drawing on a star's output
pathway.unlocks: a beam that could push sails between stars, or act as a defensive system — with the same physics cutting both ways.
